name: Gmail
summary: Google OAuth for the Gmail API. Testing with up to 100 named users is quick and needs no review. Real users need Google verification: sending is a sensitive scope (review up to 10 days), reading or modifying mail is restricted (review of several weeks plus a yearly security assessment).

paths.label: Testing with up to 100 people
paths.detail: You and listed test users, no Google review.

paths.label: Read inboxes for real users
paths.detail: Public launch that reads or changes mail.

verdicts.why: In Testing mode you and up to 100 listed test users can connect with no Google review, but their tokens expire after 7 days.
gmail.send is a sensitive scope, so a public app needs sensitive scope verification with a privacy policy, verified domain and demo video.

verdicts.handsOn: 1 to 3 days, plus a paid assessment
verdicts.waiting: Several weeks, then a reassessment every 12 months
verdicts.why: Reading or modifying mail uses restricted scopes, which need restricted scope verification and a yearly CASA security assessment by a Google-approved lab.

skip.note: Composio has a managed Google OAuth app for Gmail, so you can ship without your own verification. Google's own Gmail MCP server is in Developer Preview and needs your own OAuth client: its metadata points to accounts.google.com, which has no registration_endpoint.
whyOwnApp: Show your own app name and logo on the consent screen instead of Composio's.
Get your own API quota instead of sharing Composio's.
Extra scopes such as gmail.settings.basic can hit an 'App is blocked' screen on the managed app.

requirements.label: Google Cloud project with the Gmail API enabled
requirements.detail: The OAuth client and consent screen live in this project. Composio's docs also note the Gmail API must be enabled in the project that owns your credentials.

requirements.label: Test users listed on the consent screen
requirements.detail: While the app is in Testing, only listed test users can sign in, up to 100 of them.

requirements.label: Home page on a domain verified in Google Search Console
requirements.detail: Verify your authorized domains in Search Console with an Owner or Editor account. The home page must clearly describe the app.

requirements.label: Privacy policy on the same domain
requirements.detail: It must be public, hosted on the same domain as your home page, linked from the consent screen, and follow Google's Limited Use rules.

requirements.label: Written justification for each scope
requirements.detail: Explain why you need each sensitive or restricted scope and why a narrower one will not work.

requirements.label: Unlisted YouTube demo video
requirements.detail: Show the full consent flow, the app name, the OAuth client ID in the address bar, and how each scope is used. An agent can write the script; you record it.

requirements.label: CASA security assessment, renewed every 12 months
requirements.detail: Needed if restricted data can be reached from or through your servers. A Google-approved third-party lab does it, and you pay the lab.

steps.title: Pick the narrowest scopes and write the OAuth code
steps.detail: Use gmail.send for sending only and avoid https://mail.google.com/ unless you must delete mail permanently. Endpoints come from Google's discovery document.

steps.title: Create a Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: Sign in to the Google Cloud console, create a project and turn on the Gmail API.

steps.title: Set up the consent screen and audience
steps.detail: Choose External unless every user is in your Workspace organization, declare your scopes, and add test users while in Testing.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client ID
steps.detail: Create a web application client, add your redirect URI, and store the client secret on your server.

steps.title: Draft the privacy policy, scope justification and demo script
steps.detail: An agent can write all three from your code and data flows. You review and publish them.

steps.title: Verify the domain, record the video and submit for verification
steps.detail: Verify the domain in Search Console, upload the demo as unlisted on YouTube, set the app to In production and submit.

steps.title: Google reviews your sensitive scopes
steps.detail: Google says sensitive scope verification can take up to 10 days. Brand verification can add 2 to 3 business days if branding changed.

steps.title: Google reviews restricted scopes and you pass CASA
steps.detail: Restricted scope verification can take several weeks. The CASA assessment with an approved lab runs alongside and repeats every 12 months.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send
scopes.meaning: Send email on the user's behalf. Cannot read the mailbox.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata
scopes.meaning: View message metadata such as labels and headers, but not the body. Still restricted.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify
scopes.meaning: Read, compose and send email, and move it to trash, but not delete it permanently.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.compose
scopes.meaning: Manage drafts and send email. Restricted, unlike gmail.send.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.labels
scopes.meaning: View and edit labels. Does not read messages. No review needed.

scopes.name: https://mail.google.com/
scopes.meaning: Full mailbox access, including permanent delete. Only ask for it if you must bypass the trash.

limits.title: 100 test users while in Testing
limits.detail: An app with Testing status works only for up to 100 test users you list on the consent screen.

limits.title: Refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing
limits.detail: Test users' authorizations expire seven days after consent, unless you only ask for name, email and profile.

limits.title: 100 new users for an unverified production app
limits.detail: A production app that has not passed verification shows the unverified app screen and is limited to 100 new users in total.

limits.title: 100 refresh tokens per user per client
limits.detail: Issuing a 101st refresh token for the same Google Account silently kills the oldest one. Tokens unused for six months also stop working.

limits.title: CASA repeats every 12 months
limits.detail: Restricted scope apps must be reassessed at least every 12 months after the lab's Letter of Assessment date. Third-party labs list AL1 assessments from $3,000 to $6,000.

blockers.symptom: A user sees an access blocked or unverified app screen and cannot finish sign-in.
blockers.fix: While in Testing, add their Google account as a test user. For more than 100 users, submit the app for verification.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails with invalid_grant about a week after users connect.
blockers.fix: That is the 7-day Testing limit. Move the app to In production, which for sensitive or restricted scopes means getting verified.

blockers.symptom: Users outside your company get an org_internal error.
blockers.fix: Your consent screen user type is Internal. Switch it to External to allow any Google account.

blockers.symptom: An older connection for the same user suddenly stops working.
blockers.fix: You passed 100 refresh tokens for that user and client. Store and reuse one token per user instead of re-consenting each time.

blockers.symptom: Composio managed auth shows 'App is blocked' after you add scopes.
blockers.fix: Remove the extra scopes from the auth config, or use your own Google OAuth app that is verified for them.

sources.title: Google OpenID Connect discovery document
sources.note: Fetched live: auth endpoint accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth, token endpoint oauth2.googleapis.com/token, PKCE S256 and plain, no registration_endpoint.

sources.title: Configure the Gmail MCP server
sources.note: Developer Preview; you create your own OAuth client ID and secret.

sources.title: Gmail MCP protected resource metadata
sources.note: Fetched live: authorization_servers is accounts.google.com. /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server on gmailmcp.googleapis.com returns 404, and accounts.google.com's metadata has no registration_endpoint, so no DCR.

sources.title: Composio Gmail toolkit
sources.note: Composio-managed OAuth available: Yes. Default consent screen uses Composio's OAuth app with a shared quota.

sources.title: Leviathan Security: Google CASA assessment
sources.note: One approved lab's price list: AL1 at $3,000, $4,500 or $6,000 depending on how fast it starts. AL2 is quote only.

unverified: Exact CASA price at other labs (TAC Security's FAQ returned 403), and how long a CASA assessment takes end to end.
Whether the 100 new user cap for unverified apps ever resets; Google only says 'in total'.
The Gmail MCP metadata also lists finer scopes such as gmail.send.self and gmail.messages.readonly that are not in Google's public scope table, so their tiers are unknown.
